text: Over the last 30 days, some visitors have raised concerns about overcrowding, especially when large school groups visit simultaneously, which limits access to exhibits. Several critical reviews focused on the heavy use of AI in the exhibits, describing it as distracting or lacking educational value, with some visitors feeling it did not honor Theodore Roosevelt’s legacy. A few visitors also noted that the content did not provide enough depth about Roosevelt’s accomplishments and impact. Positive feedback often mentioned the interactive exhibits and the building’s architecture, but the balance between technology and historical interpretation may need adjustment.

windows.7: Over the past week, visitors have not raised any critical issues with the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, maintaining a high average rating of 4.95 across 21 reviews. Some comments touched on the use of AI in the exhibits, suggesting there may be room to address concerns or clarify its role. Interactive exhibits received the most attention, with several visitors noting their engagement. A few reviews mentioned the architecture and interpretation, while isolated feedback addressed food and beverage options, historical balance, dwell time, timed entry, and staff. Overall, there are no urgent problems, but monitoring AI-related feedback and food services could be beneficial.
